# Engine oil and filter change

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Warm engine, drain old oil with new washer and filter, then refill to replace the fluid. [t60]

[Unverified value] Fill the engine with 5 3/8 quarts of fresh motor oil. [t60]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Warm the engine to operating temperature if it has sat for a while.
2. [Partial] Unscrew the oil filler cap located on the front right side of the engine.
3. [Partial] Position an oil drain pan underneath the oil pan.
4. Remove the drain plug using a 14mm socket or wrench.
5. [Partial] Allow all old oil to drain completely from the pan.
6. Replace the old drain plug washer with a new one.
7. Tighten the drain plug and washer back into place.
8. [Partial] If equipped with a factory skid plate, remove two 10mm bolts holding the filter access cover.
9. [Partial] Place another drain pan under the opening to catch oil dripping from the filter.
10. Unscrew the old oil filter by hand or use an oil filter wrench if needed.
11. [Partial] Coat the new filter's rubber o-ring with fresh oil before installing it.
12. Hand-tighten the new filter and ensure the old o-ring came off cleanly.
13. [Unverified value] Use a funnel to add 5 3/8 quarts of fresh oil into the filler opening.
14. Replace the oil filler cap securely.
15. Start the engine and let it run briefly to circulate the new oil.
16. Check for leaks around the drain plug and filter while the engine runs.
17. Turn off the engine and wait a few minutes for oil to settle in the pan.
18. Remove, wipe clean, and reinsert the dipstick with its yellow top.

_Procedure reported by [t60]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-change-engine-oil-2nd-gen.4954/>_
